source.title: The Geometry of Memorization: Finite-Time Spectral Sensitivity as a Diagnostic for Flow Matching Models

record.tranche_reason: The study measures spectral collapse in continuous-time generative models trained on different data-set sizes. It does not test the listed classification, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or memorized-example-removal versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports an FTSS-based audit of generative memorization. It does not measure held-out classification error or any of the specific behaviors named in V1–V8.
record.test_reason: The study measures trajectory sensitivity in flow-matching generative models as training-set size varies. It reports none of the random-label, held-out classification, width, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, weight-perturbation, or memorized-example-removal comparisons specified by V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' conclusion that low-data training produces spectral collapse and that FTSS can audit generative memorization internally. However, the claimed absence of baseline comparisons needs qualification: the ratio and Algorithm 2 explicitly require a reference bottleneck from a model trained on the largest subset. Independent memorization detection accuracy is not reported.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates flow-matching generative models with a newly proposed FTSS diagnostic; it does not use a method comparable to the listed classification studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported spectral behavior varies with training-set size and is examined across datasets and architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the tested flow-matching architectures and datasets, the normalized FTSS bottleneck ratio increases with training-set size and reportedly approaches 1 at N ≥ 1000.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data scarcity is associated with lower normalized trajectory-sensitivity bottlenecks in the tested generative flows; the authors propose this as a memorization diagnostic.

record.problems: The empirical results use only 2 training runs per data size. The described separation is aggregate, while detailed curves are shown in figures.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. The paper describes curves and ratios in Figures 1–2, but provides no recoverable separate numeric results for each architecture, dataset, or sample size in the text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance performance under random labels using the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification test error and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under comparable tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out classifier error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures. FTSS instead measures sensitivity to intermediate-state perturbations.
Test accuracy after removing examples selected by label-memorization influence, compared with removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Architecture, optimizer, and dropout choices are experimental settings, not controlled tests of their generalization effects. Citations to original sources do not constitute tests of their claims.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label accuracy.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected classification performance.
Dropout effects on held-out classification error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to classification generalization gaps.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: Models across all tested architectures and datasets (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measured the Spectral Collapse Ratio M across training-set sizes using FTSS.

conditions.value: N swept over 50, 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 12000; imagenette capped at 5000
2 independent training runs at each data size
Flow matching with straight-line conditional probability paths

rows.baseline: Model trained on the largest subset for each dataset: 12,000 samples for MNIST/CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100; 5,000 for imagenette.
rows.value: The ratio increases monotonically with the number of samples until reaching a threshold; M ≈ 1.0 at N ≥ 1000. The paper reports completely non-overlapping variance intervals between extreme data scarcity and the fully resolved data regime.
rows.uncertainty: Mean ± standard deviation over the 2 training runs.
rows.locator: Section 3.2; Appendix A, Figures 1–2; Sections A.2 and A.5
rows.note: The text states the result across tested architectures and datasets; separate numerical values by dataset, architecture, or sample size are presented only in figures and are not reconstructed here.
rows.check: The reported ratio trend matches Section 3.2, but this trajectory-sensitivity diagnostic cannot establish any listed version. Its association with memorization is interpreted without an independent memorization or held-out-performance measure. Non-overlapping mean ± standard-deviation intervals from two runs do not themselves establish the claimed strict statistical separability.
